transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vakulman.
Authorities in Bend, Oregon say three children
and a teacher were killed yesterday
in a shooting at an elementary school.
The children were aged five, eight, and 11.
Another child and another teacher were wounded.
Police in Bend say the shooter was a 16-year-old male.
He was shot and killed by a bystander
who pursued him into the school,
and Piers Arezoo-Resvani says little
is known about the bystander.
At a press conference last night,
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek commended that bystander.
And to the community member who heroically intervened
to stop further loss of life,
your actions carry a heavy emotional burden,
and I just want you to know
that my thoughts are with you as well.
It's not clear who the community member was,
whether he was a parent or some armed passerby
who sprang into action, is not yet confirmed.
And Piers Arezoo-Resvani reporting.
Alaska's Senate race was the focus last night
as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan
faced off against Democrat
and former Congresswoman Mary Peltola.
Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin reports
the two frequently interrupted
and accused each other of lying
during their debate in the Anchorage.
Both candidates strayed from the question topics
to fight with each other.
Sullivan raised Peltola's vote
against a 2023 defense bill.
My opponent did vote against our military,
did vote against pay raise for our troops
because she wanted more transgender surgeries
for our troops.
I need to read about that.
That is an outrage.
That is absurd.
Peltola said she voted for the final bill,
increasing military pay.
I think that Alaskans have had it up to here
with the lying and the dishonesty.
Dan, you should be ashamed of yourself.
Most polls show Sullivan is lagging.
President Trump and Vice President Vance
each flew to Alaska this month to campaign for him.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
Stocks opened mixed this morning
as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh renewed his promise
to bring inflation under control.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports
the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 360 points
in early trading.
Warsh told an audience in Bangkok overnight
he and his colleagues will deliver price stability.
But as usual for the Fed chairman,
he did not offer a roadmap
of the central bank's upcoming decisions on interest rates.
Investors think the Fed will likely
hold its benchmark rate steady
when policymakers meet later this month,
then raise rates at the following meeting in December.
Warsh is optimistic that artificial intelligence
will ultimately lead to higher productivity
and lower inflation.
In the short run though,
the massive investment in AI data centers
is driving up prices for construction and computer chips.
Despite consumers' worries about inflation,
U.S. retailers are expecting a jolly holiday season
with sales of more than a trillion dollars.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Israeli government says that goods
have not entered Gaza for the last couple of days.
Israel is blaming Hamas for imposing high taxes
on Palestinian merchants.
NPR's Daniel Estrin has more.
Israel says merchants in Gaza refused to import goods
because Hamas imposed high taxes and threatened merchants.
Hamas called it a voluntary payment.
Because of the crisis,
commercial goods did not enter Gaza over the last two days,
cutting off about 50% of all shipments
of essential items to Gaza.
Market prices in Gaza have skyrocketed.
Shayna Lowe of the Norwegian Refugee Council Aid Group.
Any disruption to the flow of goods,
whether they're humanitarian or commercial,
is a shock to the system in Gaza.
In Gaza, a Palestinian trucker's union blamed Israel
for halting the shipments.
Gaza's two million people face a humanitarian crisis
with Israeli restrictions on aid supplies.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News.
Pakistan is ordering engineers
to inspect all of the country's school buildings.
That's after a school building collapsed this week,
killing more than 30 people.
Nearly all of the victims were children.
The Vatican says Pope Leo will deliver his Sunday prayer
in public as usual this weekend.
The Pontiff's doctors say he is showing continued improvement
from lung cancer surgery this week.
The Vatican released photos of Pope Leo today.
He was helping celebrate mass yesterday in the hospital.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Shooting at a Bend, Oregon elementary school kills three children and a teacher; shooter killed by bystander
Alaska Senate debate between Dan Sullivan and Mary Peltola turns into mutual accusations of lying
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh vows to control inflation; stocks open mixed
Israel says goods stopped entering Gaza for two days, blaming Hamas taxes on merchants
Pakistan orders inspection of all school buildings after collapse kills more than 30
Vatican says Pope Leo will deliver Sunday prayer in public as he recovers from lung cancer surgery
